name: Mid-year population estimates (single year of age, LA & small area)
lowest_geography: LSOA (small area population estimates, released later than LA series)
variables: population by single year of age
latest_period: Mid-2025 (LA single-year-of-age dataset NM_2002_1 updated on Nomis 29 Jul 2026)
next_release: Mid-2026 estimates expected summer 2027 (ONS: to be announced)
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Dataset NM_2002_1 (LA SYOA); small-area SAPE datasets separate.
limitations: Rolled forward from Census 2021 using admin data; international migration is the least certain component and has been revised heavily since 2023. LSOA estimates lag LA estimates and are less reliable for 16-24 (students, armed forces). Checked values: Bedford 196,398; Central Bedfordshire 321,605; Luton 236,380 (mid-2025).
why_it_matters: Denominator for every rate (NEET %, claimant %, inactivity) and the base for cohort sizing: mid-2025 16-19s = 9,076 Bedford, 13,490 Central Beds, 12,418 Luton; 18-24s = 13,292 / 19,379 / 21,884.

name: Subnational population projections for England: 2022-based
variables: projected population by single year of age and sex to 2047
latest_period: 2022-based (Nomis dataset NM_2006_1 / ppsyoala, last updated 9 Oct 2025)
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Dataset NM_2006_1 (mnemonic ppsyoala).
limitations: Trend-based, not policy-based: does not include housing growth at Wixams, Universal-induced in-migration, or the Local Plan. 2022 base pre-dates the 2023-25 migration revisions.
why_it_matters: Projects the 16-24 labour pool to 2031 (opening) and beyond; checks whether the 'young local workforce' assumption holds.

name: Annual Population Survey (APS) – local labour market indicators
lowest_geography: LA (some PCON tables; MSOA not published)
variables: employment, unemployment and inactivity rates by age
inactivity by reason (student, looking after family, long-term sick, retired, other)
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Dataset NM_17_5 (percentages, with numerator/denominator/confidence measures 20599/21001/21002/21003).
limitations: Small LA samples: Bedford 16-64 employment rate 79.7% carries a ±5.0pp 95% CI; Central Beds 20-24 inactivity and every LA's 'inactive who want a job' were suppressed (disclosive/unreliable) in the Jul25-Jun26 release. LFS response collapse since 2020 (ONS reweighting; Transformed LFS transition) raises bias risk. Year-to-year swings of several points are often noise.
why_it_matters: Only LA-level source for inactivity by reason and qualifications of the whole population (including non-claimants). Latest: inactivity 16-64 Bedford 18.7%, Central Beds 11.4%, Luton 27.8%, England 20.5%.

name: Claimant Count (JSA + UC searching for work)
publisher: Office for National Statistics / DWP (via Nomis)
variables: claimants by age band and sex
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Dataset NM_162_1.
limitations: Nomis labels it experimental (official statistics in development) because UC widened who must search for work; counts only 'searching for work' UC conditionality, so excludes most inactive and health-condition claimants. Rounded to 5. Not comparable with pre-2013 JSA series.
why_it_matters: Most timely local signal. Sep 2026: Bedford 5,465 (4.5%), Central Beds 5,150 (2.6%), Luton 10,320 (6.6%); aged 16-24: 980 / 1,090 / 1,800.

name: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE)
latest_period: 2025 on Nomis (NM_30_1/NM_99_1 updated 3 Nov 2025); ONS 2026 provisional published 22 Oct 2026, not yet loaded on Nomis at time of check
next_release: 2026 provisional on Nomis (date not confirmed); 2026 revised ~Oct 2027
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). NM_30_1 resident, NM_99_1 workplace.
limitations: 1% PAYE sample: occupational pay at LA level is mostly suppressed; excludes self-employed. Use regional SOC pay for hospitality/leisure wage benchmarking.
why_it_matters: Benchmarks Universal pay offer against local wages (Bedford resident median FT annual pay 2025 on Nomis £41,214) and tests the NLW commitment against hospitality pay.

name: Business Register and Employment Survey (BRES) – open access
lowest_geography: LSOA (rounded open-access); unrounded via Nomis licensed access
next_release: 2025 results expected autumn 2026 (not yet on Nomis at 5 Nov 2026)
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). NM_189_1 (open access); NM_172_1 etc for licensed.
limitations: Workplace-based; open-access figures rounded and small cells suppressed; excludes most self-employed and farm agriculture; volatile at LSOA. Bedford total employment 2024 = 83,000.
why_it_matters: Sizes incumbent hospitality, retail, leisure (SIC 55, 56, 93.21 amusement parks) and construction employment exposed to displacement by Universal.

name: Census 2021 topic summaries (TS tables)
variables: TS061 method of travel to work
ethnicity, country of birth, English proficiency
next_release: No 2031 census confirmed; ONS moving to admin-based population estimates
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call, free registered uid for larger pulls; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Bulk CSVs at https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/census/2021/bulk.
limitations: Taken during COVID lockdown/furlough: ONS warns travel-to-work, workplace and economic activity (furloughed counted as employed) are distorted. Cell-key perturbation alters small counts (do not sum OAs to check). Five years old by 2026.
why_it_matters: Only near-complete count of inactive non-claimants, carers and people in poor health by small area; base for LSOA-level 'hidden inactive' estimates.

name: Census 2021 multivariate (RM) tables and custom datasets
lowest_geography: OA (subject to disclosure rules, coarser categories at lower levels)
variables: economic activity x age x sex
api_notes: Create-a-custom-dataset tool (ons.gov.uk/datasets/create) and ONS 'Census Maps'; RM tables also on Nomis. Flexible tables refuse combinations that fail disclosure checks.
limitations: Disclosure control blocks many age x activity x health combinations below MSOA; same COVID caveats as TS tables.
why_it_matters: Profiles inactive 25+ by qualification and health simultaneously - the segment Universal's 'Limited Skill' roles could absorb.

name: Census 2021 origin-destination (workplace and travel-to-work flows)
publisher: Office for National Statistics (via Nomis); safeguarded detail via UK Data Service
api_notes: Public ODWP tables via Nomis; OA-level and detailed flows need UKDS safeguarded/secure licence.
limitations: Strongly depressed by home-working in March 2021; Universal's own staff distribution (34% Bedford, 35% Central Beds, 7% Luton) was modelled from existing commuting patterns and inherits this bias.
why_it_matters: Calibrates the labour catchment and how many Luton/MK residents already commute towards Kempston Hardwick.

name: ONS Open Geography Portal (boundaries, lookups, ONSPD/NSPL)
api_notes: ArcGIS REST feature services (GeoJSON) per dataset; postcodes.io is a convenient wrapper (site at 52.0898,-0.4996 resolves to LSOA E01034424 'Bedford 018H', ward Wixams & Wilstead, PCON Mid Bedfordshire).
limitations: Must keep 2011 vs 2021 LSOA codes apart (DfE and DWP products switched at different times); PCON 2024 boundaries differ from 2010.
why_it_matters: Spine for every join (LSOA21 for IoD2025/UC/Census, LAD for DfE).

name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025
publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
variables: income, employment, education & skills (children/young people and adult sub-domains), health, crime, barriers, living environment
api_notes: XLSX/CSV downloads; ranks are relative so do not compare to IoD2019 ranks without care.
limitations: Relative ranking, not absolute levels; indicator data mostly 2022-2023; employment domain counts benefit claimants so it misses non-claimant inactivity.
why_it_matters: Targets outreach to LSOAs with high adult-skills and employment deprivation within commuting range of the site.

name: Participation in education, training and NEET age 16 to 17 by local authority
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Built from NCCIS returns: quality depends on each LA's tracking; high 'not known' rates hide NEETs. Only ages 16-17 (academic age) - 18+ tracking is optional. Residence-based, so young people in Luton colleges counted by home LA.
why_it_matters: Core statutory NEET measure for the 16-17 cohort that would enter Universal's opening-year workforce (aged 21-22 in 2031).

name: Apprenticeships (starts, achievements, participation)
variables: standard/sector subject area (e.g. Construction; Leisure, Travel & Tourism; Retail & Commercial)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: ILR-based; small LA x subject cells rounded to nearest 10 and suppressed <5; in-year figures revised; learner residence not workplace.
why_it_matters: Construction made up 24.6% (280 of 1,140) of Bedford + Central Beds apprenticeship starts in 2021/22 vs 8.0% England (Universal ESP Table 8) - a strength to build on; Universal commits to 55-70 apprenticeships a year.

name: Further education and skills
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Excludes 16-18 classroom learning detail (in 16-19 performance) and non-funded/private provision; Adult Skills Fund devolution would change who reports.
why_it_matters: Measures adult re-skilling throughput (ESOL, L2 hospitality, construction CSCS-type courses) for inactive 25+ and 19-24s.

name: Key stage 4 destination measures
latest_period: 2024/25 publication (published 15 Oct 2026; covers pupils finishing KS4 two years earlier)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Two-year lag; sustained = 2 terms; employment matched via LEO-type data; small school cohorts suppressed.
why_it_matters: School-level signal of who drops out of post-16 - feeds the NEET-risk index.

name: 16-19 destination measures
variables: sustained destinations after 16-18 study (HE, FE, apprenticeship, employment)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Lagged; institution-based so out-of-area colleges (e.g. Bedford College Group, Barnfield/Luton Sixth Form) blur LA attribution.
why_it_matters: Shows the share of Level 2/3 leavers going straight into work - the pool Universal's 'Early Career' roles target.

name: Level 2 and 3 attainment age 16 to 25
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Uses NPD/ILR matching; excludes young people who left England; very small groups suppressed.
why_it_matters: Quantifies 19-year-olds without L2 English & maths - the gating qualification for many apprenticeships.

name: Children looked after in England including adoptions (incl. care leavers)
variables: care leavers aged 17-21 in education, employment or training
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Small numbers; heavy suppression at LA level for 19-21 breakdowns; LA of responsibility not residence.
why_it_matters: Universal's apprenticeship commitment reserves a portion for care leavers and signing the Care Leavers Covenant - this is the monitoring baseline.

name: Education, health and care plans
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: LA-maintained plans only; 'NEET with EHCP' counts small and not consistently recorded.
why_it_matters: Sizes young adults (to 25) with EHCPs who need supported internships - links to Universal's accessible-hiring and disability commitments.

name: Schools, pupils and their characteristics
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: School-based (not residence); academies and independent schools differ in coverage; FSM proxy for disadvantage under-counts since UC transitional protection.
why_it_matters: Year-group counts (Y7-Y11 in 2026) are the cohort that will be 18-22 at opening in 2031 - basis for roll-forward.

name: Key stage 4 performance
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Provisional then revised; Progress 8 disrupted for cohorts affected by cancelled KS2 tests (2020/21).
why_it_matters: Universal ESP cites only 40%/42% of FSM pupils passing GCSE English/maths locally vs 74%/76% non-FSM - the attainment barrier to apprenticeships.

name: 16 to 19 performance (A level, technical and vocational results)
variables: A level/applied general/tech level/T Level results
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Institution-based; T Level cohorts small; qualification reform (defunding of overlapping BTECs) breaks time series.
why_it_matters: Gauges supply of L3 technical leavers in engineering/creative/hospitality relevant to technical services and entertainment roles.

name: Get Information about Schools (GIAS)
api_notes: Daily CSV 'all establishments' extract; no auth. Join to performance tables by URN.
limitations: Administrative register; closed/merged URNs need mapping across years.
why_it_matters: Locates schools/colleges for drive-time catchments to the site and Universal's outreach targeting.

name: NEET age 16 to 24 (annual brief)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton). This publication exposes an API dataset.
limitations: LFS-based: no LA estimates; regional sampling error large.
why_it_matters: Regional benchmark for the 18-24 NEET rate the tool cannot observe locally.

name: Young people not in education, employment or training (NEET), UK
limitations: LFS quality concerns; national/regional only.
why_it_matters: Headline trend: c. 981,000 NEET 16-24 in Apr-Jun 2026; over half economically inactive.

name: Pupil absence in schools in England
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton). Weekly 'Pupil attendance in schools' (official statistics in development) gives near-real-time LA data.
limitations: School-based; severe-absence counts small at school level.
why_it_matters: Persistent/severe absence in Y9-Y11 is the strongest early predictor of later NEET - key NEET-risk index input.

name: Suspensions and permanent exclusions in England
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Excludes off-rolling/managed moves; AP pupils partly captured.
why_it_matters: Exclusion is a NEET-risk marker for the index.

name: Elective home education
variables: children known to be home educated (census day and in-year)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Official statistics in development; relies on voluntary LA registers - unregistered home-educated children are invisible.
why_it_matters: Home-educated teens often lack GCSE English/maths and drop out of NCCIS tracking at 16.

name: Special educational needs in England
variables: SEN support and EHCP pupils by primary need
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: School-based; age 16-19 coverage only in schools.
why_it_matters: SEN support (non-EHCP) pupils are a large NEET-risk group not captured in the EHCP release.

name: Longer term destinations (1, 3 and 5 years after KS4)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton). Has API dataset.
limitations: Long lag; LEO-based employment definitions.
why_it_matters: Only LA-level view of what happens to young people up to age 21 - fills the 18-21 gap in NCCIS tracking.

name: Further education outcomes (LEO-based)
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: 3-year lag; employment from HMRC PAYE only (self-employment via SA).
why_it_matters: Tests whether local adult/hospitality courses actually lead to sustained jobs.

name: Employer Skills Survey 2024
lowest_geography: LSIP area (some LA estimates with low base warnings)
variables: hard-to-fill and skill-shortage vacancies by occupation/sector
api_notes: EES has a public statistics API (https://api.education.gov.uk/statistics/docs/) but only some publications expose API datasets; otherwise download the release ZIP/CSV via the 'Download all data' link. Filter on time_period, geographic_level and new_la_code (E06000055 Bedford, E06000056 Central Beds, E06000032 Luton).
limitations: Establishment survey; local bases small; hospitality sector subsample at LSIP level unreliable.
why_it_matters: Measures existing hard-to-fill hospitality/construction vacancies that Universal will compete with.

name: DWP Stat-Xplore (UC, ESA, PIP, Carer's Allowance, Attendance Allowance, HB, NINo)
lowest_geography: LSOA (UC people; PIP/CA to LSOA or ward depending on dataset)
variables: people on UC by conditionality regime (searching, planning, preparing, no work requirements, working)
latest_period: UC to Sep/Oct 2026 (UC collection updated 2 Oct 2026); PIP to Jul 2026 (updated 15 Sep 2026)
api_notes: Open Data API (https://stat-xplore.dwp.gov.uk/webapi/online-help/Open-Data-API.html): free account, generate API key, POST JSON table queries to /webapi/rest/v1/table; rate limited; statistical disclosure control applied (random rounding).
limitations: Benefit receipt is not the same as inactivity: misses non-claimants entirely; UC conditionality groups change with policy (e.g. 2025-26 health element reforms); LSOA cells perturbed so small-area sums don't add.
why_it_matters: Essential to estimate 'hidden' inactive/NEET people (APS/Census inactive minus claimants), and to profile UC 'no work requirements' claimants by LSOA.

name: Universal Credit Health statistics
variables: people on UC with a health condition limiting work (LCW/LCWRA)
api_notes: Also in Stat-Xplore.
limitations: WCA backlog and reform shifts levels independently of underlying health.
why_it_matters: Sizes health-related inactivity among claimants aged 18-24 and 25+.

name: Children in low income families: local area statistics
variables: children (0-19) in relative/absolute low income before housing costs
api_notes: Also on Stat-Xplore.
limitations: Modelled from benefit/tax-credit data; before housing costs only.
why_it_matters: Ward-level poverty layer for the NEET-risk index and outreach targeting.

name: National Insurance number allocations to adult overseas nationals
variables: NINo registrations by nationality, age, LA
api_notes: Stat-Xplore dataset.
limitations: Flow of registrations, not stock; says nothing about qualifications.
why_it_matters: Proxy for recent migrant inflow (incl. those with unrecognised overseas qualifications) - Luton especially.

name: Earnings and employment from PAYE Real Time Information
publisher: Office for National Statistics / HM Revenue & Customs
latest_period: Flash estimate for Sep 2026 released 20 Oct 2026
limitations: Flash estimates revised; LA by residence; excludes self-employed.
why_it_matters: Timely check on whether local payroll employment grows as construction ramps up.

name: Labour demand volumes by SOC 2020 and local authority (Textkernel online job adverts)
variables: deduplicated online job adverts by 4-digit SOC 2020
api_notes: XLSX via ONS release page (https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/labourdemandvolumesbystandardoccupationclassificationsoc2020ukjanuary2017toaugust2026).
limitations: Adverts not vacancies; one advert can cover many posts (Universal mass-hiring will be undercounted); SOC assigned by text matching; replaces discontinued Adzuna series (ended 24 Oct 2024).
why_it_matters: Live monthly occupational demand in Bedford/Central Beds/Luton - baseline for hospitality and construction competition and later for tracking Universal's hiring.

name: Longitudinal Education Outcomes (LEO) record-level data
publisher: Department for Education (with HMRC and DWP)
variables: school/FE/HE records linked to PAYE employment, earnings, self-assessment, benefit spells
api_notes: Apply via DfE data sharing process; accessed in ONS Secure Research Service as an accredited researcher; outputs checked for disclosure.
limitations: Months to approve; outputs must pass SDC; no hours/occupation; 3-4 year lag. DWP's RAPID-LEO hidden-NEET method shows feasibility.
why_it_matters: Gold standard for tracking local young people from school into (or out of) work and benefits; enables the hidden-NEET method at LA level.

name: National Pupil Database (NPD)
api_notes: Apply via https://www.gov.uk/guidance/apply-for-department-for-education-dfe-personal-data; access in ONS SRS; LAs already hold their own pupils' data and can produce aggregates locally.
limitations: Lengthy approval, legal gateway needed; pupil-level outputs suppressed.
why_it_matters: Enables a pupil-level NEET-risk model; the LAs' own school census extracts offer a faster route.

name: Individualised Learner Record (ILR)
variables: aims, levels, sector subject areas, outcomes, prior attainment, employment status on entry, LLDD
api_notes: Record-level via DfE/ONS SRS; providers (e.g. Bedford College Group, Central Beds College, Luton Sixth Form/Barnfield) hold their own ILR and can share aggregates under a DSA.
limitations: Approval timescales; employment status on entry is self-reported.
why_it_matters: Lets the tool see unemployed/inactive adults entering FE in relevant subjects by postcode.

name: NCCIS / CCIS client-level tracking (young people's post-16 activity)
publisher: Local authorities (Bedford, Central Bedfordshire, Luton) reporting to DfE
variables: monthly activity codes (EET, NEET by reason e.g. illness, pregnancy, carer, not known)
api_notes: Held by each LA's tracking/careers team; LA can provide ward/LSOA aggregates and NEET reason breakdowns under a data-sharing agreement.
limitations: Statutory tracking ends at academic age 18 (to 25 for EHCP); quality depends on LA contact rates; 'not known' cohort.
why_it_matters: Only source of NEET reasons and small-area NEET locations for 16-17s; enables LSOA targeting not possible from published data.

name: Labour Force Survey / APS microdata
lowest_geography: LA (Secure Access); region in End User Licence
variables: full LFS question set: inactivity reasons, wanting work, health conditions, qualifications, caring, benefit receipt (self-reported)
api_notes: End User Licence (registration) for regional files; LA identifiers need Secure Access (accredited researcher, training).
limitations: Small LA samples; pooled 3-year APS needed for any LA x age x reason estimate.
why_it_matters: Allows bespoke estimates of inactive non-claimants by reason for Bedfordshire (pooled years).

name: ONS Secure Research Service (gateway for ILR, LEO, NPD, ASHE/BRES microdata, Census microdata)
api_notes: Digital Economy Act accredited researcher + project accreditation; remote secure desktop; output checking.
limitations: Weeks-months to set up; results must be non-disclosive.
why_it_matters: Route for any record-level linkage that the open tool cannot do.

name: HMRC PAYE RTI microdata
publisher: HM Revenue & Customs (via HMRC Datalab / ONS SRS)
variables: employment spells by employer, pay, age, residence
api_notes: HMRC Datalab application (strict legal gateway); public outputs are the ONS RTI bulletin above.
limitations: Very restricted; employer identifiability.
why_it_matters: Could track flows from existing hospitality employers into Universal (displacement) if a gateway were granted.

name: OHID Fingertips (Public health profiles)
publisher: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities
variables: employment gap for people with long-term conditions/mental illness
api_notes: Fingertips API (https://fingertips.phe.org.uk/api), R package fingertipsR; indicator IDs stable.
limitations: Many indicators re-publish other sources with lag; QOF prevalence reflects recorded diagnosis.
why_it_matters: Health barriers to work (mental health in 18-24s) by LA - relevant to the rise in ill-health inactivity.

name: Fit notes issued by GP practices
variables: fit notes 'not fit for work' vs 'may be fit'
limitations: Only GP-issued fit notes; diagnosis coding incomplete; practice not residence.
why_it_matters: Health-related work absence signal, including people who are not on benefits.

name: HESA HE Student Data - where students come from (Tables 61/62)
variables: HE enrolments by home LA and provider
api_notes: CSV open data (site blocks scripted clients - download manually).
limitations: Domicile pre-study; students studying away still counted as LA's residents in MYE only partially.
why_it_matters: Shows how many local 18-24s are in HE (and outside the labour pool), and University of Bedfordshire/Cranfield pipeline for corporate/creative roles.

name: Further education and skills inspections and outcomes: management information (Nov 2025 - Aug 2026)
variables: latest inspection outcomes (report-card framework from Nov 2025)
limitations: New report-card framework from November 2025 is not comparable with single-word judgements.
why_it_matters: Quality of local FE/apprenticeship providers that would deliver Universal-related training.

name: Journey time statistics (LSOA to employment centres)
variables: minimum journey times by PT/walk, cycle, car to employment centres, FE colleges
limitations: Pre-dates the site; employment centres defined by existing BRES clusters, not Kempston Hardwick; bespoke modelling needed.
why_it_matters: Baseline accessibility to FE colleges; method template for a site-specific catchment.

name: Bus Open Data Service (timetables, GTFS)
api_notes: Regional GTFS timetable files download without a key (https://data.bus-data.dft.gov.uk/timetable/download/gtfs-file/<region>/); the SIRI/API endpoints need a free API key. Bedfordshire operators sit mostly in the south_east file. Used for journey times to the site (travel_lsoa) via OpenTripPlanner.
limitations: Future services (Wixams shuttle, EWR) must be scenario-added; demand-responsive buses not captured.
why_it_matters: Enables realistic public-transport catchment for shift workers (early/late starts) from Luton, Bedford estates and rural Central Beds.

name: Immigration system statistics: regional and local authority data
variables: asylum seekers in receipt of support
limitations: Stocks of specific schemes only; no skills data.
why_it_matters: Identifies refugee/migrant groups with right to work but likely unrecognised qualifications and ESOL needs.

name: Universal Destinations & Experiences UK Project - Employment & Skills Plan (Document 6.12.0)
publisher: Universal Destinations & Experiences (prepared with Volterra), submitted to MHCLG
variables: operational jobs by department and FT/PT (2031, 2051)
frequency: One-off (June 2025); secured by SDO controlling documents
limitations: Promoter estimates 'sense checked' by Volterra; FT/PT split for 2051 simply mirrors 2031; staff residence modelled from 2021-era commuting.
why_it_matters: The only detailed demand profile: 8,050 direct jobs (5,950 FTE) in 2031, 49% part-time, 81% Vocational/Limited-skill roles; peak 5,380 construction workers winter 2029.

name: Environmental Statement Chapter 13 - Socio-economics (WSP)
publisher: Universal Destinations & Experiences / WSP, submitted to MHCLG
lowest_geography: LSOA (Local Area = 12 LSOAs within 500 m of site)
limitations: Uses HCA Additionality Guide defaults (displacement 5-25%, multipliers 1.1-2.2) plus a visitor-induced uplift benchmarked to Disneyland Paris; gross 2051 direct jobs (12,465) differ from the ESP (10,000).
why_it_matters: Defines the official study areas and net-jobs arithmetic the business case must reconcile with.

name: Special Development Order: Entertainment Resort Complex and Associated Development in Bedford (conditions & discharges)
publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
variables: discharged conditions (construction management plans, mass grading, flood resilience, Broadmead Road crossing)
limitations: Planning documents, not workforce data; construction phasing must be inferred from discharged packages.
why_it_matters: Best public signal of construction progress (and so timing of labour demand).

name: South Midlands Local Skills Improvement Plan (LSIP 2.0, 2026-2029)
publisher: Northamptonshire Chamber with Milton Keynes and Bedfordshire Chambers of Commerce (ERB)
lowest_geography: LSIP area (Bedford, Central Beds, Luton, MK, North & West Northants)
variables: priority sectors (IS-8 + construction + health & social care; food/drink/hospitality)
limitations: Qualitative/employer-survey based; cites Universal UK and Luton Airport as major projects but no quantified Universal demand.
why_it_matters: Statutory employer-led skills plan that Universal's ESP commitments reference (SEM LSIP 2023); 2.0 names Universal UK for construction, hospitality, creative and design skills.

name: Bedford Borough Council - Employment and skills overview
limitations: Policy statement; the Universal ESP notes Bedford has no standalone employment & skills strategy.
why_it_matters: Host authority's stated priorities; Bedford also hosts the Universal resort information page (https://www.bedford.gov.uk/business/invest-bedford/universal-united-kingdom-resort).

name: Central Bedfordshire Council - Skills for All Strategy
latest_period: Consulted Jan-Apr 2024 (successor to Education and All Age Skills Strategy cited by Universal ESP)
limitations: Strategy, not data; check adopted version.
why_it_matters: Central Beds supplies an estimated 35% of Universal's opening-year staff.

name: Luton 2040 and Luton Employment & Skills Strategy 2022-27
latest_period: Luton 2040 progress report Jan 2025; new economic strategy launched 2025
limitations: Strategy, not data.
why_it_matters: Luton has the highest inactivity (27.8%) and claimant rates in the sub-region but only ~7% of Universal staff are modelled to come from Luton - a transport/inclusion gap.

name: Young People and Work: interim report and analytical annex (Milburn review)
publisher: Department for Work and Pensions (independent review)
limitations: Exploratory RAPID-LEO + LFS method; England-level only.
why_it_matters: Estimates ~314,000 of ~678,000 NEET 18-24s in England (46%) claim no benefit - the method template for a local hidden-NEET estimate.

name: False starts: the UK's growing NEETs problem
limitations: National analysis of LFS.
why_it_matters: Finds nearly half of NEETs claim no benefits and sickness/disability share of NEETs has more than doubled since 2005 - supports the hidden-NEET gap.

name: Learning and Work Institute - young people research and NEET commentary
limitations: Mostly national; some regional.
why_it_matters: Evidence that only about 1 in 4 NEET young people get Jobcentre Plus support (Nov 2025 commentary).

name: Youth Futures Foundation data dashboard
limitations: Repackages LFS/APS - same small-sample issues.
why_it_matters: Ready comparator views for 16-24 outcomes; also hosts the Youth Employment Toolkit evidence on what works.

name: Institute for Employment Studies - labour market briefings and research
limitations: National.
why_it_matters: Evaluation evidence on reaching inactive people (e.g. local Get Britain Working trailblazers).

name: Centre for Cities data tool
lowest_geography: Primary Urban Area (Bedford, Luton, Milton Keynes)
variables: employment rate, claimant rate, qualifications, productivity, wages by city
limitations: PUA geography differs from LAs; Central Beds largely outside PUAs.
why_it_matters: Benchmarks Bedford and Luton against comparable towns.

name: Lightcast job postings analytics
variables: job postings by SOC/SIC, employer, skills, salary, qualifications
api_notes: Paid licence/API; many LAs and colleges already subscribe.
limitations: Commercial black box; adverts not vacancies; licence restricts publication of raw counts.
why_it_matters: Employer-level, skills-level demand data; could detect Universal and contractor postings as they appear.

name: Indeed Hiring Lab job postings tracker
variables: job postings index vs Feb 2020 baseline by occupational category (e.g. food preparation & service, hospitality & tourism, construction)
api_notes: Open CSVs on GitHub (CC-BY 4.0); commentary at https://www.hiringlab.org/uk/.
limitations: Index not counts; national.
why_it_matters: Timely national read on hospitality hiring appetite - context for displacement risk.

name: CITB Construction Workforce Outlook 2026-2030 (formerly Construction Skills Network)
variables: annual recruitment requirement by occupation (28 groups)
api_notes: Excel data file on the page; regional detail via interactive chart filters.
limitations: Regional only; model-based; major projects may not be fully in the pipeline.
why_it_matters: UK needs ~206,000 extra construction workers 2026-30 (41,200/yr, 1.6% of 2025 workforce) - the competing demand into which Universal's 5,380 peak arrives.

name: UKHospitality workforce and employment-cost evidence
variables: hospitality employment, vacancies, youth share of employment
limitations: Advocacy body; figures often from ONS/RTI reworked; press-reported numbers vary.
why_it_matters: Reports hospitality as a major first-job sector for 16-24s and recent job losses after employer NICs rises - shapes competition for and availability of entry-level staff.

name: London Luton Airport expansion DCO decision (Luton Rising)
limitations: Promoter figures; phased to 2040s.
why_it_matters: Major competing demand for Luton's labour (aviation, hospitality, security, logistics).

name: Census 2021 barrier-to-work measures: car/van availability (TS045), English proficiency (TS029), household composition (TS003), general health (TS037)
variables: households with no car or van (TS045 cat 1 / all households)
residents aged 3+ who cannot speak English well or at all (TS029 cats 4+5)
lone-parent households with dependent children (TS003 cat 10 / all households)
residents in bad or very bad general health (TS037 cats 4+5)
next_release: No 2031 census confirmed; ONS moving to admin-based population estimates
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). Datasets NM_2063_1 (TS045, dim C2021_CARS_5), NM_2048_1 (TS029, C2021_ENGPRF_6), NM_2023_1 (TS003, C2021_HHCOMP_15), NM_2055_1 (TS037, C2021_HEALTH_6); measures=20100. Fetcher: pipeline/fetch_census_barriers.py -> site/data/census_barriers.json.
limitations: Cell-key perturbation makes small LSOA cells (<10) unreliable, notably English proficiency and lone parents. Car availability is a household measure (not licences or individual access). General health is not age-standardised (TS037ASP / NM_2092_1 gives age-standardised LA rates). COVID lockdown timing; five years old by 2026 and Luton has grown since.
why_it_matters: Practical barriers for a site at Kempston Hardwick with shift work and limited public transport: households without a car are 25.0% in Luton, 18.2% Bedford, 11.3% Central Beds (BEDS 17.1%, England 23.5%); 5.5% of Luton residents (12,000) cannot speak English well or at all vs 1.9% England; 19,075 lone-parent households with dependent children across the 3 UAs (6.9%); 30,000 residents in bad/very bad health (4.3%).

name: BRES employees in competing entry-level sectors: warehousing & support for transport (SIC 52), land transport (49), air transport (51), wholesale (46)
api_notes: Nomis REST API v01 (https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/api/v01/help); CSV/JSON/SDMX; no key needed for <25k cells per call; use geography TYPE codes (e.g. TYPE154 = 2023 LADs, TYPE151 = LSOA 2021). NM_189_1, industry codes 146800692 (52), 146800689 (49), 146800691 (51), 146800686 (46); employment_status=1 (employees), measure=1. Added to pipeline/fetch_nomis_la.py BRES section -> bres_sectors (bres_emp_/bres_share_/bres_lq_ warehousing, land_transport, air, wholesale).
limitations: Divisions 49/51/52 are subsets of section H (existing bres_*_transport) - do not add them together. Open-access counts rounded (Bedford and Central Beds air transport round to 0). Workplace-based; jobs are allocated to the reporting unit's location; airport operation and ground handling (52.23) sit in division 52, not 51.
why_it_matters: Universal will recruit from the same entry-level pool as the M1/A421 logistics belt and Luton Airport: warehousing & transport support employs 14,500 across the 3 UAs (LQ 2.1; Central Beds 8,000, LQ 3.2; Bedford 4,000, LQ 2.1), air transport 4,000 in Luton (LQ 12.8), land transport 6,000 and wholesale 14,500 (2024).

name: People on Universal Credit by conditionality regime (Stat-Xplore UC_Monthly)
lowest_geography: Census 2021 Output Area (pipeline requests LSOA21, falls back to MSOA21)
latest_period: Not yet fetched (no API key on this machine)
api_notes: Open Data API https://stat-xplore.dwp.gov.uk/webapi/rest/v1 with free key in an APIKey header. database str:database:UC_Monthly; measure str:count:UC_Monthly:V_F_UC_CASELOAD_FULL; fields F_UC_DATE:DATE_NAME, V_F_UC_CASELOAD_FULL:COA_CODE (National - Regional - LA - OAs, 2021 MASTERGEOG21 valuesets), V_F_UC_CASELOAD_FULL:CCCONDITIONALITY_REGIME. Rate limit 2,000 requests per window. Fetcher: pipeline/fetch_dwp_uc.py (key from STATXPLORE_API_KEY, /etc/beds/statxplore.key or ~/.config/beds/statxplore.key; --dry-run prints queries; --schema prints discovered ids).
limitations: Fetcher written and unit-tested offline but not yet run against the live API. Statistical disclosure control perturbs cells (small LSOA cells noisy, components may not sum). 'No work requirements' mixes health (LCWRA), carers, parents of under-1s, students and over-SPA claimants. Legacy benefits (ESA, IS, JSA) excluded. Latest month provisional.
why_it_matters: Most current small-area count of benefit-recipients not expected to work (the inactive-on-UC pool) and of in-work claimants who must seek more hours - both target groups for Universal's part-time, entry-level roles.

name: House price to residence-based earnings ratio (median and lower quartile)
variables: median and lower-quartile residence-based full-time earnings
latest_period: 2025 (house prices year ending Sep 2025; ASHE April 2025)
api_notes: Single workbook aff2ratioofhousepricetoresidencebasedearnings.xlsx at a stable /current/ URL; tables 5c (LA median) and 6c (LA lower quartile), 1c/2c (region, England). Parsed with zipfile + xml.etree.
limitations: Full-time residence-based earnings, not young entrants' pay; LA earnings are ASHE survey estimates with sampling noise. 2025 median ratios: Bedford 8.37, Central Bedfordshire 8.36, Luton 9.07 vs East of England 8.52 and England 7.64; lower quartile Bedford 9.10, Central Beds 9.35, Luton 9.81 vs England 6.99.
why_it_matters: Entry-level (lower-quartile) home ownership is less affordable in all three UAs than in England, which shapes whether NLW-paid resort staff can live near the site.

name: Price Index of Private Rents (PIPR): monthly average private rents by LA
api_notes: Latest workbook link scraped from the dataset page (dated folder, e.g. /21october2026/); Table 1 long format, time period as Excel date serial.
limitations: Stock of existing tenancies, so new-let rents a newcomer pays are typically higher; latest months provisional. Sep 2026 average rent: Bedford GBP 1,177 (1-bed 802), Central Bedfordshire 1,258 (870), Luton 1,231 (913); England 1,466 (1,199), East of England 1,298 (900).
why_it_matters: A one-bed private rent in the three UAs takes 39-44% of gross full-time NLW pay (GBP 24,784.50 a year), so housing cost is a real barrier to in-migrating workers.

name: Childcare providers and inspections: management information
variables: latest inspection outcomes (renewed EIF report-card areas and legacy grades)
next_release: Next quarterly extract (30 Sep 2026 data expected late 2026)
api_notes: Latest 'childcare provider data as at <date>' CSV found via the GOV.UK content API (https://www.gov.uk/api/content/government/statistical-data-sets/childcare-providers-and-inspections-management-information).
limitations: Management information, not official statistics. Excludes maintained nursery schools/classes, so understates early education capacity; places are registered capacity, not vacancies or hours. 30 Jun 2026: EYR places per 100 children aged 0-4 Bedford 42.9, Central Bedfordshire 39.5, Luton 25.4 vs East of England 46.0, England 43.8.
why_it_matters: Childcare capacity constrains how many economically inactive parents (25+) could take shift work at the resort; Luton has markedly fewer registered places per child.

name: GMCA Unit Cost Database v3.0 (fiscal value of moving claimants into work; NEET costs)
variables: fiscal benefit of UC jobseeker into work
NEET cost per year (fiscal and economic)
api_notes: Workbook https://www.greatermanchester-ca.gov.uk/media/sbdg15pr/gmca-unit-cost-database-v3-0-final.xlsx, sheet 'Employment & Economy'; values extracted to research/unit_costs.json.
limitations: Fiscal values are transfers (excluded from public value); NEET rows are 2010/11-based and rated lowest confidence; ESA value is 2017/18 modelling uprated; no UC health-claimant value. UC jobseeker into work GBP 17,736/yr, ESA claimant GBP 15,470/yr, NEET 18-24 GBP 6,325/yr fiscal (2025/26 prices).
quality: Curated secondary unit costs (HM Treasury Green Book supplementary guidance)
why_it_matters: Gives a defensible GBP value per local resident moved from benefits into resort jobs for the business case.

name: Local-hire outcomes at comparable large developments (compiled)
publisher: Various (DCMS Olympic meta-evaluation, LLDC, Battersea Power Station, Center Parcs, Disneyland Paris impact study, Eden Project)
api_notes: Compiled by hand into research/local_hire_benchmarks.json, each entry with its own source URL.
limitations: 'Local' is defined differently in every case (host boroughs, single borough, county, 15-mile radius), so shares are not directly comparable; several are operator claims, not independent monitoring. Center Parcs Woburn Forest (2014, 1,500 jobs): 90% live within 15 miles; London 2012 ODA construction: 17.5% host-borough residents vs 15% target; Westfield Stratford: ~3,000 unemployed Newham residents vs 2,000 target.
quality: Mixed: evaluation reports and monitoring data alongside operator press statements
why_it_matters: Benchmarks what a realistic local-recruitment target for the resort's ~8,050 operational jobs could be, and how much it depends on how 'local' is defined.

name: Bus Open Data Service regional GTFS timetables (south_east, east_anglia, east_midlands)
publisher: Department for Transport (Bus Open Data Service)
variables: registered bus timetables (GTFS: stops, routes, trips, stop_times, calendars)
frequency: Daily regeneration of the regional GTFS files
latest_period: Feeds downloaded 5 Nov 2026 (services valid from 5 Nov 2026); modelled day Tue 17 Nov 2026
api_notes: Regional GTFS zips download without an API key: https://data.bus-data.dft.gov.uk/timetable/download/gtfs-file/<region>/ (region e.g. south_east, east_anglia, east_midlands). Bedfordshire's operators (Stagecoach East, Arriva Beds & Bucks, Grant Palmer etc.) are mostly in the south_east file (about 2,200 Bedfordshire/Luton stops); east_anglia and east_midlands add cross-boundary routes. Used in pipeline/fetch_travel.py with OpenTripPlanner 2.8.1 (Docker batch).
limitations: Bus only (no rail). Published schedules, not punctuality; demand-responsive and works services often missing; a route can appear in more than one regional file. Future services (resort shuttles, EWR) are not in it.
quality: Statutory operator registrations published by DfT; data-quality varies by operator
why_it_matters: The bus network for LSOA-to-site public transport journey times (travel_lsoa: arrive by 08:30, home after a 22:30 shift).

name: OpenStreetMap Bedfordshire extract (street network for walk, cycle, car routing)
variables: roads, paths, cycleways, access restrictions, speed limits
api_notes: https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/united-kingdom/england/bedfordshire-latest.osm.pbf; used by OpenTripPlanner (UK tag mapping) in pipeline/fetch_travel.py.
limitations: Ceremonial-county clip: walking/driving just over the Herts/Bucks/Cambs/Northants border is not routable. Car speeds are free-flow from tags/defaults (no congestion).
quality: Crowd-sourced; road network in England is near-complete
why_it_matters: Walk access to stops and car/cycle journey times to the Kempston Hardwick site. Licence ODbL 1.0 (attribution: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors).

name: Rail timetables for Bedfordshire lines (Marston Vale, Thameslink, EMR) - hand-built GTFS
publisher: London Northwestern Railway; Thameslink (GTR); East Midlands Railway (published timetables)
frequency: Timetable changes each May and December
api_notes: No openly licensed, registration-free GB rail GTFS was found (the RDG/Network Rail timetable feeds need registration). pipeline/travel/rail_gtfs/ holds a small GTFS: Marston Vale trains transcribed from the LNR PDF by pipeline/travel/make_rail_gtfs.py; Thameslink and EMR Bedford-Luton as frequencies.txt headways; station coordinates from NaPTAN (https://naptan.api.dft.gov.uk/v1/access-nodes?dataFormat=csv&atcoAreaCodes=910).
limitations: Thameslink/EMR departures are approximate (regular headways, peak fast trains omitted); Marston Vale bus replacement during East West Rail works is not modelled; no other rail lines.
why_it_matters: The site sits next to Kempston Hardwick station; Luton/Leagrave/Flitwick residents reach it by changing at Bedford, so rail determines Luton's public transport catchment.
